review_candidates.title: Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer
review_candidates.description: Job Summary The Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer will support STRIDES activities in Banten Province to strengthen veterinary laboratory capacity for detecting zoonotic diseases with pandemic potential, particularly Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI). The officer will provide hands-on technical support to strengthen HPAI diagnostic capacity, particularly real-time PCR testing at UPTD PPV Banten. The role includes supporting laboratory testing readiness, quality management, biosafety and biosecurity, specimen management, and timely laboratory reporting. The officer will also support coordination and monitoring of HPAI laboratory testing for surveillance activities in priority districts, particularly Lebak and Tangerang. Working closely with the Senior Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer, STRIDES team, and government counterparts, the officer will support laboratory assessments, assist in addressing identified gaps, and monitor progress in implementing agreed improvements to improve the timeliness of HPAI detection, reporting, and outbreak response in line with the 7-1-7 target. This is a full-time, Banten-based position requiring regular on-site work at UPTD PPV Banten and close coordination with provincial and district government counterparts. Responsibilities/Duties Technical Requirements: Provide hands-on technical support to strengthen veterinary laboratory capacity for HPAI detection, particularly real-time PCR testing. Support laboratory testing readiness, including equipment functionality, reagent and consumable availability, quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), and implementation of standard operating procedures (SOPs). Support laboratory assessments and assist laboratory personnel in addressing identified gaps through practical improvements, technical training, and mentoring. Monitor progress in implementing agreed recommendations and corrective actions and report challenges requiring further support. Support the implementation of laboratory quality management, biosafety, and biosecurity practices to improve diagnostic quality and laboratory safety. Work with laboratory personnel and STRIDES technical teams to identify additional needs and coordinate appropriate technical assistance. Specimen Management, Referral, and Laboratory Reporting: Support coordination and monitoring of HPAI sample submission and laboratory testing from priority districts, particularly Lebak and Tangerang. Work with laboratory personnel and government counterparts to strengthen coordination of specimen collection, transportation, receipt, documentation, and referral procedures. Support timely laboratory testing, result reporting, and communication with relevant government counterparts. Assist with laboratory data management and reporting through relevant information systems, including IVLab and iSIKHNAS, as applicable. Identify challenges that may delay sample submission, laboratory testing, or result reporting, and support practical solutions to improve timely disease detection and response. Project Implementation and Coordination: Work closely with provincial and district livestock services, veterinary laboratories, DIC Subang, and other relevant government partners. Support coordination between laboratory diagnostics, surveillance, and outbreak response activities, including efforts to improve performance against the 7-1-7 target. Assist in planning, implementing, and monitoring STRIDES laboratory strengthening activities in Banten Province. Participate in technical meetings, laboratory assessments, training, and field visits as required. Identify implementation challenges, communicate them to the Senior Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer, and support agreed follow-up actions. Monitoring, Documentation, and Reporting: Monitor progress of laboratory strengthening activities against agreed work plans, recommendations, and deliverables. Maintain accurate records of technical activities, laboratory support, and follow-up actions. Prepare technical reports, presentations, meeting summaries, and implementation updates for STRIDES and relevant stakeholders. Support collection and analysis of laboratory performance data to inform program monitoring and decision-making. Problem Solving & Impact Identifies technical and operational challenges affecting laboratory testing and reporting. Works with laboratory personnel and STRIDES technical teams to develop practical solutions. Exercises sound judgment and raises technical or implementation issues to the Senior Laboratory and Diagnostic Officer when needed. Contributes to improving laboratory readiness, diagnostic quality, and timely HPAI detection and reporting. Qualifications Knowledge & Skills: Good understanding of laboratory diagnostic practices, particularly molecular diagnostics and real-time PCR. Knowledge of laboratory QA/QC, SOP implementation, biosafety, biosecurity, and specimen management. Ability to identify laboratory capacity gaps and support practical improvements. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, particularly when working with government laboratory personnel and other stakeholders. Ability to coordinate activities, monitor progress, and follow up on agreed actions. Good organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently while maintaining close coordination with the STRIDES technical team. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and basic laboratory data management. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Veterinary Medicine, Veterinary Laboratory Science, Microbiology, Medical Laboratory Technology, Biological Sciences, or a related field. A veterinary background is strongly preferred. A minimum of 4 years of relevant professional experience in laboratory diagnostics or laboratory systems strengthening, preferably in veterinary or infectious disease diagnostic laboratories. Academic internships, university laboratory assistant roles, and laboratory activities conducted as part of academic studies do not count toward the minimum experience requirement. Demonstrated hands-on experience in molecular diagnostics, particularly real-time PCR, including sample processing, quality control, and interpretation of test results. Knowledge of zoonotic diseases with epidemic and pandemic potential, particularly avian influenza, is highly desirable. Experience implementing laboratory QA/QC, SOPs, biosafety, and biosecurity practices. Experience supporting laboratory assessments, technical training, mentoring, or laboratory capacity strengthening is an advantage. Experience working with government laboratories, veterinary services, or public health programs is preferred. Familiarity with laboratory information systems and specimen referral networks is an advantage. Previous experience with donor-funded projects, particularly U.S. Government-funded programs, is desirable but not required. Strong organizational, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills. Good working proficiency in English and Bahasa Indonesia, including the ability to prepare technical reports and communicate effectively with project teams and government counterparts. Working Conditions and Travel Requirements: This position is based in Banten Province. The successful candidate must reside in Banten Province or be willing to relocate. Regular on-site work at UPTD PPV Banten is required to support HPAI laboratory testing and capacity strengthening. The position requires a combination of office-based, laboratory-based, and field-based work. Ability to spend long hours looking at a computer screen and performing repetitive keyboard tasks. Ability to sit and stand for extended periods. Ability to lift or move up to 5 lbs. Approximately 10–25% local and regional travel may be required for laboratory assessments, coordination, and field activities. The officer is expected to comply with FHI 360 policies, professional standards, and workplace requirements. Full-Time Employment Commitment This is a full-time position requiring full commitment to FHI 360 and the STRIDES Activity during regular working hours, including on-site work at UPTD PPV Banten, participation in STRIDES meetings, laboratory visits, and other assigned activities.
